title: Cryptographic Misuse: Weak PRNG, Fast Hashes, Non-constant-time Compare
platform_conditions: CPython 3.x standard library (random, hashlib, hmac, secrets)
security_mechanism: random seeds a Mersenne Twister from a 32-bit-derived state and emits enough state bits through its outputs to reconstruct the generator, so tokens, reset codes, or keys drawn from random are predictable from a few observed values. md5/sha1 applied directly to passwords give fast, unsalted digests that tolerate massive offline guessing; hmac.compare_digest exists precisely because '==' on MACs short-circuits and leaks a timing oracle that recovers the tag byte by byte.

source_sink_clues.source: The security value itself: session tokens, password reset codes, API keys, MAC tags, password digests chosen by the developer's library call.
source_sink_clues.sink: random.choice/random.random/randint feeding tokens or keys; hashlib.md5/sha1 used for password storage; == / != comparisons of digests or MAC tags

tracking_guards: Require secrets.token_hex/token_bytes for any security value; require hmac.compare_digest for authenticator comparisons; require a salted, deliberately slow KDF (hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac with sufficient iterations, or an Argon2/bcrypt implementation) for password storage.
not_candidate_when: random is used only for non-security purposes (sampling, shuffling, simulations), the fast hash digests untrusted content for integrity or deduplication rather than authentication, or the compared digests come from hmac.compare_digest already.
public_references: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/327.html
PEP 506: Designing secrets-aware standard library modules — https://peps.python.org/pep-0506/
